topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's focus on the mechanisms controlling the initiation and resolution of inflammatory immune reactions.

topics.label: Pathogen sensing via PAMPs, DAMPs, and pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects infection and cellular damage through molecular patterns and pattern recognition receptors such as Toll-like receptors and inflammasomes.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover how activated sentinel cells orchestrate leukocyte recruitment and lymphatic drainage, as well as the detrimental consequences when systemic inflammation leads to septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inflammatory responses are resolved, how damaged tissues are repaired, and what happens when unresolved inflammation leads to chronic disease or granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of next topic
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on the complement system.
